s1.syndrome_frame: Acute vision loss and eye pain with signs of intraocular inflammation
salient_findings: Blurry vision and pain in one eye
Whitish focal granuloma at the pupillary margin
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 50s
Symptoms started 4 days prior to presentation
Recent routine dental cleaning 1 week prior
No history of gingival disease or cavities
Visual acuity was 20/25 OD and 20/50 OS initially
Intraocular pressures were 15 mm Hg OD and 11 mm Hg OS
Left eye examination showed conjunctival hyperemia and keratic precipitates
Gram stain revealed gram-positive cocci in chains and gram-positive rods
Aerobic culture revealed Streptococcus intermedius
Blood and urine cultures were unremarkable
Electrocardiogram and echocardiogram were unremarkable

differentials: Acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy
per_call: Acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy

shortlist.label: Infectious endophthalmitis
shortlist.why_kept: Gram stain and culture revealed Streptococcus intermedius, consistent with bacterial endophthalmitis

shortlist.label: Endogenous endophthalmitis
shortlist.why_kept: Recent dental cleaning may have introduced bacteria into the bloodstream, leading to endogenous infection

shortlist.label: Streptococcal endophthalmitis
shortlist.why_kept: Specific type of infectious endophthalmitis caused by Streptococcus intermedius, supported by culture results

shortlist.label: Exogenous endophthalmitis
shortlist.why_kept: Possible introduction of bacteria during dental cleaning, although less likely given the lack of direct ocular trauma

shortlist.label: Bacterial endophthalmitis
shortlist.why_kept: Broad category of infection that includes Streptococcal endophthalmitis, supported by clinical presentation and lab results

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including blurry vision and pain in the left eye, along with the findings of conjunctival hyperemia, keratic precipitates, and a whitish focal granuloma, are consistent with infectious endophthalmitis. The gram stain and aerobic culture results revealing Streptococcus intermedius further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Endogenous endophthalmitis
rejected.why: The recent dental cleaning and lack of systemic infection suggest an exogenous source of infection, making endogenous endophthalmitis less likely

rejected.label: Streptococcal endophthalmitis
rejected.why: While Streptococcus intermedius was identified, this option is too specific and does not encompass the full scope of the infection

rejected.label: Exogenous endophthalmitis
rejected.why: This option is plausible given the recent dental cleaning, but it is less specific than infectious endophthalmitis

rejected.label: Bacterial endophthalmitis
rejected.why: This option is too broad, as it does not account for the specific findings and culture results in this case
